 Judgment

Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondent, who is the owner of Car bearing No.KA-50-P-8968,
alleging that on 15.07.2023 at 12.30 a.m., midnight when driving Autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AL-0217 from Koramangala Club towards Printo side, near House No.77, 17th 'E' Main road, VI Block, Koramangala, driver of the Car bearing No.KA- 50-P-8968 drove the same negligently in the same direction, dashed the same to rear part of the Autorickshaw, made the Autorickshaw to turn turtle, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at St.John's Hospital, Koramangala.
3. Regarding the accident, Adugodi Traffic police registered a case in crime No.111/2023 against the driver of the car.
4. As on the date of accident, petitioner being aged about 21 years, used to earn Rs.30,000/- p.m. by working as Auto Driver.

5. In response to the notice, respondent appeared through her Advocate, filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age, occupation and income of the petitioner, nature, consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 12.03.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 15.07.2023 at about 12.30 a.m., near House No.77, 17th 'E' Main road, 6th Block, Koramangala, Bengaluru city, he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Car bearing registration No. KA- 50-P-8968 as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

7. On 30.09.2024 and 19.12.2024 petitioner deposed as P.W.1 and produced 15 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.15.
8.
On 29.04.2025 learned Advocate appeared for the petitioner submitted arguments.
On 29.04.2025 respondent herself submitted arguments and submitted readiness to pay medical expenses on humanity grounds.
9. I have perused the entire records.

sentences.text:
On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative; Issue No.2 ...
Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.2,98,025/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. towards compensation from respondent.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- In the evidence affidavit petitioner stated that on 15.07.2023 at 12.30 a.m. midnight when driving Autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AL-0217 from Koramangala Club towards Printo side, near House No.77, 17th 'E' Main road, VI Block, Koramangala, driver of the Car bearing No.KA-50-P-8968 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to rear part of the Autorickshaw,
thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
12. In the written statement respondent denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

13. Ex.P.2 is the copy of the order sheet pertaining to C.C.No.4465/2024 on the file of MMTC - IV registered against respondent owner/driver of Car bearing No.KA-50- P-8968 on the basis of final report filed by Adugodi traffic police in Cr.No.111/2023 for having committed offence punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC and Section 185 and Section 146 r/w Sec.196 of IMV Act, in which respondent/driver of the Car pleaded guilty and suffered sentence of payment of fine.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of Accusation recorded in C.C.No.4465/2024 by MMTC-VI against respondent/driver/owner of the Car bearing No.KA-50-P-8968.

Ex.P.4 is the copy of Charge Sheet filed by Adugodi Traffic police in Cr.No.111/2023 against respondent/driver of car bearing No.KA-50-P-8968 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC and Sections 185, 146, 196 of IMV Act.

Ex.P.5 is the copy of FIR pertaining to crime No.111/2023 registered by Adugodi Traffic police against the driver of Car bearing No.KA-50-P-8968 for having committed offence punishable under Sections 279, 337 of IPC and Section 185 of IMV Act, on the basis of statement of petitioner.
FIR shows that the police have wrongly noted identification of the vehicle which caused accident as 'KA-01-AL-0217' instead of 'KA-50-P-8968'.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.8 to 10 are the copy of notice issued under Section 133 of M.V.Act, by the Investigating Officer to the respondent and reply.
Ex.P.11 is the copy of Wound Certificate in which reason for the injuries is noted as 'alleged RTA on 15.07.2023 at 12.25 a.m. opposite Koramangala Club.
Ex . P.12
is the copy of Motor vehicle Accident report.
14. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason, mode and consequence of accident.

15. Hence, I have concluded that on 15.07.2023 at 12.30 a.m. midnight, when petitioner was driving Autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AL-0217 from Koramangala Club towards Printo side, near House No.77, 17th 'E' Main road, VI Block, Koramangala, respondent negligently drove the Car bearing No.KA-50-P-8968 which had no insurance coverage, dashed the same to the rear part of the Autorickshaw, made the Autorickshaw turn turtle, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to Sanjay M C vs Regina Agnes Ambrose on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99064056/

sentences.text: Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered L3 Vertebral body fracture, severe injuries to hand, legs, head, took treatment at St.John's Medical College hospital from 15.07.2023 to 18.07.2023 by spending Rs.4,50,000/-.
Petitioner stated that, as on the date of incident used to earn Rs.30,000/- p.m. by driving Autorickshaw.
17. In the written statement, respondent denied the allegation regarding age, occupation and income of the petitioner, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

18. Wound certificate, prescriptions, medical bills and X-ray shows that in the accident petitioner suffered CT lumbar spine L3 Vertebral body fracture, lacertion over left parietal region of scalp,
small left parietal scalp hematoma, took treatment at St.John's Medical College hospital from 15.07.2023 to 18.07.2023 by spending Rs.91,025/-.
In the medical records age of the petitioner is noted as 21 years as on the date of incident.
19. In this case, there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding nature of injuries suffered in the incident, length, place and nature of treatment.
In this case petitioner not produced documentary evidence regarding his occupation and income.

Considering the nature of injuries suffered, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, I award compensation under the following heads:
Sl
. No .
Heads of Compensation Amount Rs.

1) Pain and agony 60,000.00 2) Treatment charges 91,025.00 3) Conveyance, nourishment and 6,000.00  attendant charges 4) Loss of income during treatment 96,000.00  period (Rs.16,000/- x 6)
5) Loss of amenities and future 45,000.00  unhappiness:
 Total: 2,98,025.00 20.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.2,98,025/-
with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. towards compensation from the respondent/owner/driver of the Car bearing No.KA-50- P-8968.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondent shall deposit the compensation amount within 4 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
